blend_reference_note: LWFloatBlend's buffer path (float32, vForce transfer) against float64 sRGB transfer functions and the source-over compositing equation wrapped around LWFloatBlend.mix, per straight extended-linear channel, relative to max(1, |expected|). The per-mode formulas are not transcribed a second time (that comparison would be tautological); their semantics are checked by the property tests listed under blend_extended_rules_note. 2e-5 bounds float32 pow round trips (~6e-7 each) with margin.

blend_extended_rules.Color Burn: b >= 1: b; s <= 0: lo; otherwise max(lo, 1 - (1 - b) / s).
blend_extended_rules.Screen: 1 - (1 - b)(1 - s) while b <= 1 and s <= 1; otherwise max(b, s). Never below max(b, s) for non-negative operands; continuous at 1.
blend_extended_rules.Color Dodge: b <= 0: b; s >= 1: hi; otherwise min(hi, b / (1 - s)).
blend_extended_rules.Overlay: Hard Light with the operands exchanged: HardLight(s, b).
blend_extended_rules.Soft Light: b > 1: b (above white the backdrop is kept; the in-range result at b = 1 is 1 for every s); otherwise the W3C formula, with D(b) = sqrt(b) for b > 0.25 and the cubic below.
blend_extended_rules.Hard Light: s <= 0.5: 2 b s; 0.5 < s <= 1: Screen(b, 2 s - 1) with the extended Screen; s > 1: max(b, s).
blend_extended_rules.Vivid Light: s <= 0.5: Color Burn(b, 2 s); otherwise Color Dodge(b, 2 s - 1), each with its extended rule.
blend_extended_rules.Pin Light: s <= 0.5: min(b, 2 s); otherwise max(b, 2 s - 1), unclamped.
blend_extended_rules.Hard Mix: b + s >= 1: hi; otherwise lo (a threshold, discontinuous by definition).
blend_extended_rules.Exclusion: b + s - 2 b s while both operands are in [0, 1]; otherwise |b - s|. Never negative; continuous at 0 and 1.
blend_extended_rules.Divide: s > 0: min(hi, b / s); s <= 0: hi for b > 0, lo for b < 0, 0 for b = 0.
blend_extended_rules.Hue: W3C SetLum(SetSat(s, Sat(b)), Lum(b)) with ClipColor to [lo, hi] instead of [0, 1].
blend_extended_rules.Saturation: W3C SetLum(SetSat(b, Sat(s)), Lum(b)) with ClipColor to [lo, hi].
blend_extended_rules.Color: W3C SetLum(s, Lum(b)) with ClipColor to [lo, hi].
blend_extended_rules.Luminosity: W3C SetLum(b, Lum(s)) with ClipColor to [lo, hi].

blend_extended_rules_note: Each mode's rule outside [0, 1], in encoded (sign-mirrored sRGB) operands b (backdrop) and s (source); lo = min(0, b, s), hi = max(1, b, s). Identical to LWFloatBlend.extendedRules (checked by FloatRendererPrecisionTests.everyModeDeclaresItsExtendedRule). Property tests check, for every mode: non-negative operands never give a negative result, no finite input (negative, zero, subnormal, huge, any alpha) gives NaN or infinity, every continuous mode is continuous across 1 (and 0), Screen and Lighten never fall below max(b, s), and inside [0, 1] Core Image's kernels are reproduced (blend_core_image_in_range_abs).
blend_core_image_in_range_note: For straight inputs inside [0, 1] LWFloatBlend reproduces the Core Image kernels the float compositor used before (rendered in an RGBAf context with an extended sRGB working space), per straight extended-linear channel. Measured agreement is below 1e-5; GPU float pow/division rounding and unpremultiplying a low-alpha result are allowed up to 2e-4.
tile_parity_pointwise_note: Blend modes, opacity, masks, pointwise adjustments and layer placement are evaluated per pixel from document coordinates; tiled and whole-frame evaluations must agree bit for bit. Placement of a resampled layer (rotation, scale, flip, fractional origin) uses LWFloatCompositor.resampled, whose samples depend only on document coordinates; measured 0 for every transform in FloatRendererPrecisionTests.tiledPlacementMatchesWholeFrameEvaluation.
document_region_parity_note: A document evaluated tile block by tile block (LWDocumentTileRenderer) against LWFloatCompositor.renderPlane of the whole frame, for every blend mode over a rotated, partly transparent layer and for masks, folder masks and opacity, clipping, document-anchored noise and layer effects. Core Graphics resampling depends on the context it draws into, so regions are widened out to the 256 px tile grid: every placement range is then the same document rectangle in both evaluations. Measured 0 (bit identical) on the fixtures; the bound leaves 1e-5 relative to max(1, |expected|) for float rounding.
document_region_spatial_note: Gaussian and motion blur adjustment layers are Core Image operators. Each region is widened by LWDocumentTileRenderer.halo (4 sigma + 4 for Gaussian, twice the motion radius + 16 for motion) and filtered at its document position (LWFloatCoreImage.render origin: the region's bottom-left in the whole document's Core Image coordinates), so Core Image samples and tiles it on the same grid as a whole-document render. Measured on the high-contrast HDR fixture (a 0 to 3.2 step every 97 px), relative to max(1, |expected|): Gaussian sigma 6 exactly 0, motion distance 40 at most 2.9e-4 (Core Image's motion kernel still rounds differently near the region's edge); before the region was placed at its document position these were 0.3% and 2.1%. The bound is 1e-3: 3.4 times the measured motion difference, ten times tighter than S08's 1% Core Image blur tolerance, and it fails if the document placement is dropped (measured 0.89% then).
display_conversion_note: Working samples rendered by GPUCanvasRenderer into the canvas drawable format (rgba16Float) for extended sRGB and extended Display P3 targets, against the analytic conversion. Half float keeps 11 significant bits (4.9e-4 relative); Core Image's conversion adds float rounding. Values above 1 and below 0 must survive. With the screen's EDR headroom given (maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue, read every frame), components above it saturate at it (as the display clips them, and inside half float's range); negative components are kept. The canvas re-derives its target when its window changes screen (NSWindow.didChangeScreenNotification) as well as on backing-property changes.
tile_cache_budget_note: LWDocumentTileRenderer.defaultBudgetBytes: 256 MiB of float tiles (full resolution and pyramid levels; 1024 tiles of 256x256 RGBA32F) for the interactive canvas, shared by every open document and keyed by document. It is reclaimable: when another consumer of the source-graph working set (export, RAW decode, history) cannot be admitted, least-recently-used tiles are evicted first (LWFloatReclaimable).
texture_budget_note: GPUCanvasRenderer.textureBudgetBytes: 512 MiB of cached layer and stroke textures (RGBA8 / R8). Admitting a texture evicts least-recently-used layer textures, then stroke textures no frame is drawing any more; only what the current frame draws can hold the cache above the budget.

large_document.note: A procedural 16384x12160 document (199 MP, the largest 16384-wide document DocumentLimits.maxSurfacePixels admits) of two full-size layers whose pixels are generated on demand (Multiply at 75% opacity) plus an Exposure adjustment is never allocated whole: its 3 GiB float frame cannot be resident. Tiles are evaluated in blocks of at most 1024x1024 px; returned tiles and every placement crop are charged to the working set. The cache is given 32 MiB; peak admitted working-set bytes (cache plus every evaluation lease) must stay at or below 96 MiB, and the process's physical footprint (Core Graphics and Core Image allocations included) may grow by at most 384 MiB. Measured: 48 full-resolution tiles through the 32-tile cache, 48.5 MiB peak working set, 158 MiB footprint growth (cold process) or 4 MiB (warm); a zoomed-out 4.2 MP view at level 3 built from 64 full-resolution tiles, 33 MiB, 133 MiB; a full-size layer rotated 7 degrees, 16 tiles, 29 MiB, 133 MiB. Decoding the whole layer for a tile instead (an uncropped placement) is refused by the working set. The texture cache is given 64 MiB while 1 GiB of textures is requested.

resampler_reference_note: LWFloatCompositor.resampled (bilinear at the pixel centre; High quality: the mean of n x n bilinear taps over the pixel's footprint, n the reduction factor rounded up) on smooth HDR, out-of-gamut, partly transparent content, on interior samples, relative to max(1, |expected|). Against the continuous content at the pixel's image position: measured at most 3.2e-3 (3x reduction) and 9e-4 otherwise. Against Core Graphics drawing the whole layer into one context: measured at most 3.4e-2 (Core Graphics' high-quality filter is not bilinear); Core Graphics' high-quality 3x reduction of an extended float image is excluded because it returns alpha far from the content (0.82 where the content is 0.27). Core Graphics is not used for resampled placement because its resampling depends on the extent of the image it draws: a cropped draw differed from an uncropped one by up to 15% on the same content, so no tiling could reproduce a whole frame. The bound 0.05 holds both references.
raster_fast_path_note: A plain raster layer is placed straight from its image (never materialized as a whole float plane). Placement converts the crop it reads to premultiplied extended-linear float before resampling, so an 8-bit sRGB raster that is rotated or scaled is interpolated on linear samples exactly as the earlier path (a float plane of the whole image, then placement of that plane). Measured 0 for 8-bit rotated, reduced and integer placements and float rotated and reduced placements; the bound allows the plane's straight/premultiplied round trip.
canvas_frame_budget_note: LWDocumentTileRenderer.frameBudgetBytes: one assembled canvas view, premultiplied extended-linear half float (8 bytes a sample), at most 128 MiB (16 MP, a full-resolution 5K screen). The canvas picks the pyramid level for its zoom (the coarsest level at least as fine as the display) and coarsens it further until the view fits; the whole document is never rendered or held for display.
